problem: Mapless RGB-only zero-shot ObjectNav methods (ZSON, PixNav) decide from the current observation only, with no exploration history. They fall into local deadlocks, circling in regions that semantically resemble the target location. Depth- or map-based alternatives need extra sensors and localization.
motivation: Household robots and virtual agents usually have only RGB input, so depth- and metric-map-dependent methods are hard to deploy. The authors observe that LLMs over-rely on object-room priors (e.g., a living room for a sofa), so the agent stays in an already searched area. Adding a short exploration history should fix this.
key_idea: Parse six-view panoramic RGB (plus dot-matrix images) with an MLLM into local and global text descriptions, and feed a bounded FIFO queue of past global summaries to an LLM decision maker to avoid revisiting explored areas.
insight: Two ablations show where the gain comes from. Decoupling MLLM parsing from LLM decision-making beats a one-step MLLM decision (35.0 SR vs 38.5 SR with parsing but no memory). Memory adds a further 5 SR points (38.5 to 43.5). In the deadlock test, memory raises SR from 12.0 to 48.0 and escape rate from 32.0 to 82.0. Six views matter a lot: three views drop SR to 19.5. Note that the deadlock test is small (5 hand-picked episodes x 10 runs).
method: Panoramic capture: six RGB views at 60° intervals at each waypoint; only RGB, no depth/GPS/map.
Dot-matrix preprocessing: each view is converted with Scaffold (SCA) into a dot matrix image; the RGB image supplies geometric distance cues and the dot matrix supplies planar position cues.
Local directional parsing: an MLLM (Qwen2.5-VL) outputs per-direction object list, room type, spatial relations (a merged spatial relation graph in text), information richness and target likelihood.
Global panoramic summary: the MLLM outputs a detailed overview, total objects and room type for the current surroundings, giving implicit self-localization.
Dynamic Bounded Memory Queue: FIFO queue of the last n global summaries; it is appended at each new waypoint and the oldest is dequeued once full, and it is fed to the LLM only after it is full.
LLM decision-making: DeepSeek-V3 takes local descriptions, the global summary and the memory queue and outputs a direction and a target-found flag.
Motion controller: PixNav's pixel-guided navigation skill executes the chosen direction (actions: Stop, MoveAhead 0.25 m, Turn ±30°, LookUp/LookDown).

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL (MLLM parser, frozen) + DeepSeek-V3 (LLM decision, frozen) + PixNav controller
setting.observation: six-view panoramic RGB only (60° intervals), no depth/GPS/compass
setting.action_space: discrete: Stop, MoveAhead 0.25 m, TurnLeft/TurnRight 30°, LookUp, LookDown

results: PanoNav reaches 43.5 SR and 23.7 SPL on 200 HM3D val episodes. This beats the closest RGB-only mapless baselines PixNav (37.9/20.5) and ZSON (25.5/12.6), and its SR exceeds several map-based or closed-set methods (FBE, SemExp, Habitat-Web, ESC, VoroNav). It still trails VLFM (52.2 SR, 30.4 SPL), ImagineNav (53.0 SR) and OVRL (62.0 SR).
limitations: Evaluated on only 200 HM3D val episodes with a simulator-only setup; the deadlock test uses just 5 hand-picked episodes.

Six-view panoramic capture costs extra observation steps and relies on large MLLM/LLM calls (Qwen2.5-VL, DeepSeek-V3), which adds latency; memory stores only text summaries, not multimodal or spatial information.
Still well below map-based or depth-based SOTA such as VLFM and ImagineNav; PixNav is used as the low-level controller.
